$comment: Curated card copy for each public repo. Live numbers (stars, language, last push) are fetched from the GitHub API at runtime; anything that fails to load renders as an em dash rather than a guess.

profile.tagline: Twenty-nine years in IT, one year writing code in public.
profile.role: Technical services director at an MSP

repos.name: NetReady
repos.title: NetReady
repos.tagline: Browser-native network diagnostics that never invent a number.
repos.blurb: A full diagnostics suite built on plain web APIs: fetch, WebSockets, RTCPeerConnection, the Performance Timeline, DNS-over-HTTPS. The rule that shapes the whole codebase is that when a measurement fails it reports “—” and tells you why. An earlier generated version happily produced an A grade on a machine with no internet at all; the postmortem for that is in the repo.
highlights: One-button triage answers “is it me or the internet?” with ranked causes and fixes
Offline deterministic rules engine: no model, no backend, no account
Every third-party host it touches is documented in a table in the README

repos.name: Universal-AI
repos.title: Universal AI
repos.tagline: An idle game about optimization, and about who is doing it.
repos.blurb: You etch NPU chips one at a time, buy a fab, then fifty, set a price and chase demand. Then you hand the wheel to an autonomous Overseer (a deterministic scorer, or Llama 3.2 1B running on your GPU through WebGPU), give it directives, and watch it drift. A tribute to Frank Lantz’s Universal Paperclips. Play the original first.
highlights: The simulation is a pure reducer, tick(state, now, rng): no React, no timers, no DOM
A headless run drives it to the victory condition in about half a second, as the regression guard for “this game can be finished”
docs/LESSONS-FROM-AI-STUDIO.md catalogues the seven recurring failure shapes in the generated draft

repos.name: jbl
repos.title: Joseph's Battle Lab
repos.tagline: A Pokémon damage calculator that shows its working.
repos.blurb: Stat explorer, damage calculator and family league tracker. Every step from base stats to the sixteen possible damage rolls is visible, because the point is to make the maths legible rather than hide it behind one number. The full dex is generated at build time and committed; the app never calls PokéAPI at runtime.
highlights: Sixteen-roll damage spread, fully derived on screen
Family league tracker for actual household bragging rights
Ships with a 52-Pokémon sample set; one script pulls the full dex

repos.name: ai-plays-as-ai-making-paperclips
repos.title: AI Plays as AI Making Paperclips
repos.tagline: A local LLM agent playing Universal Paperclips through the DOM. No API required.
repos.blurb: An Ollama-backed ReAct agent playing a game about an AI obsessed with paperclips. Absurd on purpose, and a genuine proof of concept for LLM-driven browser automation where no API exists. No devtools protocol, no game hooks: DOM observation, click injection via a userscript, and a local model making decisions in a loop. The same architecture applies to any web tool that never exposed an interface.
highlights: Runs entirely on a local model: no API key, no per-token cost
Built live on Twitch, with 100% of stream ad revenue donated to Breakthrough T1D
Written up honestly, including what the agent is bad at

repos.name: luddite-gestures
repos.title: Luddite Gestures
repos.tagline: Edit Hyprland touchpad gestures on Omarchy and see which swipes will never fire.
repos.blurb: A panel for configuring Hyprland touchpad gestures on Omarchy. Shows every configured swipe and tells you which ones are physically impossible on your hardware — three-finger swipes on a two-finger trackpad, that sort of thing. Fixes the problem where you set up an elaborate gesture scheme and half of it silently does nothing.
highlights: Lists all configured gestures with their physical requirements
Detects hardware capability and flags gestures your trackpad can never trigger
Edits the Hyprland config in place with a live preview

repos.name: ascii-save
repos.title: ASCII Save
repos.tagline: ASCII and braille screensaver workshop for Omarchy, seeded with the Giants collection.
repos.blurb: A screensaver engine that renders ASCII and braille art on the terminal, seeded with the complete Giants collection. Double as a workshop for creating and previewing your own screensaver content. Drop in an image, get braille; drop in text, get ANSI art. Built for the kind of desktop where a blank screen is a wasted screen.
highlights: Complete Giants ASCII art collection included out of the box
Braille rendering for high-resolution terminal displays
Workshop mode for creating and previewing new screensaver content

repos.name: kitty-come-home
repos.title: Kitty Come Home
repos.tagline: AI-powered lost pet finder that works offline and in a crisis.
repos.blurb: An offline-first web app for finding lost pets. Generate printable flyers, search local databases, and coordinate with neighbours — all without an internet connection. Built for the moment you discover a missing pet and your phone has two bars of signal. Supabase-backed when online, fully functional when not.
highlights: Offline-first: every core feature works without a network connection
Generates print-ready lost pet flyers from a photo and description
Supabase sync when connectivity returns, no data lost in the gap

repos.name: hopper-day
repos.title: Hopper Day
repos.tagline: August 14: the day computers started speaking human.
repos.blurb: An open-source celebration of Grace Hopper’s birthday and the moment computers learned to speak human languages. A GitHub Pages landing page with the history, the significance, and the connection to the modern AI era. MIT licensed because Grace would have wanted it that way.
highlights: GitHub Pages landing page with the full history of Hopper’s contribution
Celebrates the throughline from COBOL to modern AI coding assistants
MIT licensed, designed to be forked and re-skinned for your own events

repos.name: gpg
repos.title: Grace's Playground
repos.tagline: A browser playground for experimenting with Grace Hopper’s legacy.
repos.blurb: An interactive browser-based playground. Small, focused, and fun — the kind of project that exists because an idea was too good not to build. Hosted on GitHub Pages so there’s nothing to install.
highlights: Runs entirely in the browser, no backend required
Hosted on GitHub Pages for zero-cost deployment
MIT licensed

repos.name: NeverDrop
repos.title: NeverDrop
repos.tagline: Road to Vostok mod that removes drop-on-collide for carried items.
repos.blurb: A mod for Road to Vostok that removes the frustrating drop-on-collide behaviour with carried items. Because losing your carefully scavenged gear to a physics glitch is not the kind of challenge the game designers intended. Simple, focused, and does exactly one thing well.
highlights: Removes drop-on-collide for all carried items
Compatible with the latest Road to Vostok build
Godot-native, no external dependencies

repos.name: Memory-Wall
repos.title: Memory Wall
repos.tagline: The memory wall, documented. NPU, DRAM and storage R&D, rigorously sourced.
repos.blurb: An open knowledge base on the memory wall: NPU compute, DRAM bandwidth, storage hierarchies, and the R&D timelines behind them. Every claim is cited, every source linked outward. Covers the hardware development histories that marketing materials skip, and maps honestly where public knowledge ends and speculation begins. Built for learners and for whoever builds the next entrant.
highlights: Annotated bibliographies with every claim traced to a primary source
Hardware development histories from DRAM generations through NPU architectures
Honest maps of where public knowledge ends — no speculation presented as fact

repos.name: opinionated-omarchy
repos.title: Opinionated Omarchy
repos.tagline: Personal Omarchy config, curated and documented with a rationale for every change.
repos.blurb: A fork of Omarchy with personal tweaks to window management, theming and workflow. Every change comes with a commit message explaining why, not just what — designed to be browsed on GitHub Pages before you decide whether to adopt any of it. The kind of dotfile repo that teaches by showing its reasoning.
highlights: Each config change is a separate, documented decision
Browsable as a GitHub Pages site before you clone anything
Focused on Hyprland workspace rules, keybinds and theme choices

repos.name: omarchy-fleet
repos.title: Omarchy Fleet
repos.tagline: Manage a fleet of Omarchy machines from a single source of truth.
repos.blurb: Fleet management for Omarchy: declare the state you want across multiple machines, and let the tooling converge on it. Think Ansible for your desktop fleet — package lists, config files, and dotfile state, all version-controlled and auditable. Built for anyone running more than one Omarchy box who got tired of manually keeping them in sync.
highlights: Declarative machine state with version-controlled configuration
Package and config management across multiple Omarchy installs
Audit trail: every change is a commit, every rollback is a revert

repos.name: omarchy-fleet-iso
repos.title: Omarchy Fleet ISO
repos.tagline: Build custom Omarchy ISOs for fleet provisioning.
repos.blurb: Generates bootable Omarchy ISOs pre-configured with your fleet settings. Point it at your fleet config, get an ISO that boots into a fully configured Omarchy install. Eliminates the manual setup step when spinning up a new machine in the fleet.
highlights: Generates bootable ISOs from fleet configuration
Pre-installs packages and applies config on first boot
Designed for rapid provisioning of identical Omarchy machines

repos.name: omarchy-fleet-pkgs
repos.title: Omarchy Fleet Packages
repos.tagline: Package mirror for Omarchy Fleet, keeping fleet machines on vetted versions.
repos.blurb: A private mirror of omacom/omarchy-pkgs for Omarchy Fleet (D16). Pins package versions so fleet machines don’t break when upstream moves. Acts as the single source of package truth for fleet provisioning and updates.
highlights: Pinned package versions prevent surprise breakage across the fleet
Mirror of upstream omarchy-pkgs with fleet-specific patches
Used by fleet provisioning to guarantee reproducible installs

repos.name: Opsvibe-Homepage
repos.title: This Page
repos.tagline: The homepage you are reading, listed by the same rules as everything else.
repos.blurb: Three files and a JSON blob: no framework, no bundler, nothing to keep patched. The project copy lives in data/repos.json; language, stars and last-push are pulled from the public GitHub API on load. It felt dishonest to exempt it from its own list, so here it is.
highlights: Any public repo missing from repos.json is appended straight from the API, so new work appears here without an edit
When the API call is rate-limited, the stats read “—” and say why, the same rule the rest of these projects are built on
Deployed from the repository root by GitHub Actions, gated on repos.json parsing
